title: Download selection roles
contract: The installation guide identifies account Licenses & Packs, Live-version and operating-system selectors, and Download. Its macOS Universal choice has an Intel High Sierra exception; actual package compatibility and download outcome are ungraded.

title: macOS package interaction
contract: The macOS guide names opening the downloaded .dmg, dragging the Live icon to Applications when prompted, then closing and ejecting the installer. These are publisher workflow inputs, without an installation or filesystem-success oracle.

title: Windows Live 12 installer roles
contract: For Live 12 and 11 on Windows the guide names ZIP extraction, Ableton Live [Version Edition] Installer.exe and its wizard, with C:\ProgramData\Ableton\ as the recommended default. The two Data.cab files need no further extraction. Live 10 Setup.msi is a separate predecessor branch.

title: First-launch authorization entry
contract: The guide launches installed Live from Applications on macOS or Start on Windows and describes a first-launch authorization prompt. First-launch here requires independently established unconfigured state, not an inferred factory default.

title: Edition-specific installer selection
contract: The FAQ describes a separate installer for each Live edition, including Lite/Intro upgrades to Standard/Suite. Select the intended edition package; no entitlement, upgrade eligibility or legal right is established here.

title: Multiple-version installation context
contract: The FAQ describes Live versions as independently installed and removal of an older version as optional. This source context supplies no coexistence, registration, shared-state or uninstall file-preservation oracle.

title: Online authorization entry
contract: The online guide requires an installed computer with internet and browser, then names Authorize with ableton.com in the launch dialog as a browser entry point. Browser recommendations are advice, not an exclusive support matrix.

title: Online account and license selectors
contract: The guide names account sign-in if needed, a license dropdown and View serial numbers. Upgraded-license dropdowns show the highest included version in the described example; earlier-version options do not establish entitlement.

title: Online return and confirmation controls
contract: The guide names Authorize as returning focus to Live and, conditional on successful authorization, a confirmation with OK. This conditional description does not promise successful authorization or a particular failure prompt.

title: Offline code entry and Save role
contract: The offline guide names No Internet on this computer, a hardware-code display and Save for exporting its information. The code format, identity mechanism and text-file bytes remain unknown.

title: Offline dialog revisit
contract: The offline guide locates the dialog again through Preferences Licenses / Maintenance or Licenses & Updates. Tab names are documented alternatives; version/platform-specific exact visibility remains U.

title: Offline account generation inputs
contract: The offline guide uses an internet-connected computer, selected license and offline authorization, then hardware-code entry and Download for a computer-specific .auz file. The connected computer can be the same or another computer. No generated-file, entitlement or protocol oracle follows.

title: Offline authorization file entry
contract: The offline guide describes transferring the authorization file if necessary, then opening Live and double-clicking the .auz file or dragging it onto the authorization dialog. Acceptance, machine binding, file syntax and resulting authorization state are ungraded.

title: Offline Browser Packs restriction
contract: The offline guide states Browser Packs updates and downloads are disabled when Live is authorized offline. This concerns the named Browser roles, not every Pack source or account download.

title: Automatic update menu choices
contract: The help article locates Get Automatic Updates under Maintenance in Licenses/Maintenance or, as of Live 12, Licenses & Updates. Choices are Always, Ask Me and Never. Its automatic-update default is source-described, not an observed target factory value.

title: Ask Me and Never visible policy roles
contract: Ask Me is described as prompting for a new version. Never is described as suppressing automatic download and new-release notification. Prompt identity, scheduling and actual network absence remain unknown.

title: Automatic update activation boundary
contract: Always, or accepted Ask Me, is described as downloading available updates with Live open and internet active; installed changes take effect after restart, with the updated version at next launch. Actual download/install/restart timing and success remain ungraded.

title: Manual update path
contract: The update guide routes a manual update to account download and installation. Uninstalling the current version first is not a documented prerequisite; this does not define installer transactions or safe removal behavior.

title: Scoped Windows transition exception
contract: The automatic-update article specifically requires a manual Windows transition from Live 12.2.7 to 12.3 or later, with automatic updates described as resuming afterward. This historical source branch is not a universal target update law.

title: Scoped peripheral-driver exception
contract: The article describes manual Windows installation for Push 3/Move drivers and warns that automatic installation of Live 11.3.x or 12.1.x may omit those drivers. Driver archive alternatives are source context, not hardware or driver-install evidence.

title: Plug-in scan troubleshooting modifier
contract: The crash guide instructs holding ALT/OPTION during relaunch until Live loads to temporarily disable initial plug-in scanning. Successful launch only makes a plug-in cause likely; it does not prove causation or disable all plug-in processing.

title: Temporary default Set troubleshooting entry
contract: The crash guide describes holding SHIFT while launching to temporarily open the default Set as a template diagnostic. A successful launch may point to the current template; this is not a diagnosis guarantee or permanent template reset.

title: macOS reset path inputs
contract: For Live 11 and later, the reset guide closes Live, opens Finder Go with Option and Library, then the current version under Users/[username]/Library/Preferences/Ableton. It moves Preferences.cfg and the Undo folder if present to Desktop. The example version is not a literal 12.4.3 path.

title: Windows reset path inputs
contract: For Live 11 and later, the guide closes Live, uses Explorer %AppData% and Users\[username]\AppData\Roaming, then Ableton/current-version/Preferences. Preferences.cfg and Undo if present are moved to Desktop. No deletion or atomic restore is implied.

title: Reset template entry point
contract: For the Live 11-and-later reset sequence, the guide names Browser Library/Templates/DefaultLiveSet.als, its Set Default Live Set context action, then relaunch. Existing project requirements own default-Set behavior; this adds the reset-workflow entry only.

title: Reset affected-state source context
contract: The guide describes reset as clearing Preferences including audio/MIDI, Template Set and Undo History, requiring custom hardware, plug-in folders, I/O names and settings to be re-enabled or re-entered. Exact defaults, serializable state and restored output are unknown.

title: Reset diagnostic return path
contract: The guide moves selected files to Desktop for diagnosis and suggests moving them back if resetting did not solve the issue. It does not promise a cure or complete byte-identical restoration. No file is moved or deleted here.

title: Recovery prompt and declined-recovery context
contract: The recovery article describes an undo file as usually triggering recovery. If recovery is not automatic or No was chosen on restore document, relevant files are moved into a Crash preferences folder. Usually/often wording is not a universal trigger or recovery guarantee.

title: Recovery version and platform locations
contract: The recovery guide requires the same Live version that created the undo file. It lists Windows Users\[Username]\AppData\Roaming\Ableton\Live x.x.x\Preferences\Crash\ and macOS Users/[Username]/Library/Preferences/Ableton/Live x.x.x/Crash/. x.x.x denotes the crashing version.

title: Recovery candidate item selection
contract: The guide names BaseFiles, CrashRecoveryInfo.cfg and Undo, with crash dates/times in names, selecting the matching crash if several exist, and removing the dates before the move step. This is not a file-format or guaranteed-recovery contract.

title: Version platform and edition applicability
contract: Exact 12.4.3 control availability, defaults, localization, OS/build support, edition eligibility and target prompts remain unknown. Current help revision dates are not application version proof.

title: Update save compatibility ownership
contract: The help minor-version compatibility/save-prompt descriptions need matched version evidence. Existing project older-major Save As and ALS container accepted-version contracts remain authoritative within their scopes; no minor-version law is added.
source_claim: Current help says Sets saved in newer minor versions cannot open in earlier versions and describes Save As/new-version prompts.

title: Installer and updater filesystem outcomes
contract: Package verification, installed-file changes, installer cancellation, partial writes, uninstall preservation, permissions and transaction boundaries are unknown.
source_claim: The Windows installation guide warns against storing personal content in the application installation folder because uninstall/update can lose that content.

title: Authorization negative and persistence outcomes
contract: Invalid/expired/mismatched authorization, unowned or absent entitlement, code/file errors, server refusal, revoked session, retry/cancel, restart persistence and account-state effects are unknown.

title: Authorization update and usage-data internals
contract: Hardware-code derivation, .auz syntax, signatures, credentials, network protocol, telemetry/consent payload, updater service/private helper and rollback mechanism are unspecified. Static helper categories are not runtime evidence.

title: Update failure cancellation and policy persistence
contract: Release discovery, consent cancellation, disconnected operation, policy persistence, partial download/install, interrupted restart, rollback and diagnostic outcomes remain unknown.

title: Reset persistence and restoration outcomes
contract: Actual default values, Undo History clearing boundaries, default-template identity, audio/MIDI output, failure handling, saved Set effects and restoration completeness remain unknown. Existing project Undo History/default-Set requirements are not replaced.

title: Recovery destination ambiguity
contract: The article move step parenthetical Parent folder (Preferences -> Ableton -> Live x.x.x.) does not resolve cleanly against both earlier OS-specific locations. Preserve it as source context; do not synthesize a destination or a guaranteed Replace prompt.
source_claim: The article says to move renamed items to its Parent folder, choose Replace if offered, then start Live; recovery should trigger again.

title: Recovery success and decline boundaries
contract: Successful project recovery, exact restored edits/undo/automation/media, malformed or missing items, repeated crashes, decline/retry, cancellation and output identity are unknown. Existing project/persistence failure obligations stay open.

title: Unsaved recorded audio recovery
contract: Recoverability and content of unsaved recorded audio remain unknown. The guide says it may or may not be recoverable and gives macOS Live Recordings/Temp Project and Windows local Temp search locations only.
source_claim: The guide points to Users/Username/Music/Ableton/Live Recordings/Temp Project on macOS and C:\Users\USERNAME\AppData\Local\Temp\ on Windows, without promising recovery.

title: Crash diagnosis and support outcomes
contract: A crash/hang category, successful diagnostic launch, report content or support request does not establish a cause or fix. Contact/report entry points are context only; nothing is sent and no private report encoding or data payload is specified.
source_claim: The guide distinguishes sudden shutdown from a frozen process, and says crash-report email alone does not create a support request.

title: Transport rate restart and teardown
contract: Install/update/auth/reset/recovery interactions with playback, recording, unsaved automation, sample-rate changes, shutdown and teardown have no supported outcome oracle.

title: Resource source loss and malformed baselines
contract: Unavailable media, package/config/recovery source loss, offline account and permission/resource boundaries have no newly established outcome. Existing media and export error owners retain their unknowns.

title: Uninstall and service operations
contract: Detailed uninstall, license transfer/deactivation, device/account management, authentication security and OS repair workflows are outside the retained article bodies and unknown here. Linked articles are not captured evidence.

title: Timing and performance
contract: No installation/update/authorization/recovery duration, progress ratio, retry schedule, CPU/disk cost or response-time tolerance is established.
